title: eviction-aware-idle-latch-smoother-for-continuous-batcher
author: Asha Kaur
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent starvation for small, latency-sensitive requests when continuous-batcher windows overlapped with KV-cache eviction churn. In short bursts the batcher would hold slots in an 'idle latch' state waiting for a soft fill and those latches were being prematurely reclaimed or left pinned during eviction/rehydration, which amplified tail latency. This PR introduces an eviction-aware idle latch smoother and a lightweight backpressure inspector to reduce starvation and improve fairness without materially increasing median latency.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce 'idle_latch_smoother' heuristic in the continuous batcher scheduler: when a slot becomes idle we now track an eviction-resilience score derived from recent KV-cache miss/reload events and request size distribution. The smoother delays aggressive reclamation for slots with high resilience scores and ages the delay with an exponential decay so long-running fairness isn't compromised. 2) Add a small, low-overhead 'backpressure inspector' thread that scans the admission queue at controlled intervals to detect cohorts (groups of requests) that are repeatedly losing slots due to eviction thrash; it emits metrics and triggers an adaptive grace window. 3) Make kernel-selection hints tolerant to transient descriptor invalidation during KV rehydration so the runtime avoids a costly synchronous fallback path. 4) Add a KV-cache pin telemetry span and counters so the scheduler can correlate eviction events with batch slot churn. 5) Safety: the smoother is conservatively gated behind a config flag and defaults to off for dedicated/private customers unless explicitly enabled via runtime tuning.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler heuristic implementation and unit tests - [x] End-to-end perf test harness for microburst workload - [x] Telemetry and dashboards updated - [x] Feature gated and documented - [x] Rollout/rollback plan in PR description

Why this is different from prior work: Prior PRs focused on deadline-based admission windows and slot rebalancing. This change specifically targets the interaction between KV eviction/rehydration and idle-slot reclamation: instead of only counting time-based idleness, the scheduler reasons about eviction noise and request cohort continuity to avoid oscillation that disproportionately affects small requests.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: The runtime flag 'batcher.eviction_idle_smoother' is off by default. We will enable in canary for 2 clusters, monitor the new metric 'batcher.eviction_churn_cohort_loss_rate' and rollback if cohort loss increases by >5% in the first hour. Rolling upgrade plan is described in the rollout_notes field.

Metrics added (observability): batcher.eviction_churn_cohort_loss_rate, batcher.idle_latch_smoother_active, batcher.smoother_eviction_rescore_histogram, kv.pin_rehydrate_latency_ms. Dashboards updated: /dashboards/continuous-batcher/eviction-smoother.json

Safety and performance notes: Microbenchmarks show 95th p99 reduced by ~18% on the tested microburst profile with a <1% change in median. CPU overhead measured at +0.3% on coordinator threads with the smoother enabled.

release_notes: Introduce eviction-aware idle latch smoother to reduce starvation caused by KV-cache eviction churn. Opt-in via batcher.eviction_idle_smoother flag. Recommended for latency-sensitive microburst workloads. Metrics and dashboards included.
rollout_notes: Canary enable on two low-traffic clusters for 24h. Watch batcher.eviction_churn_cohort_loss_rate and p99 latency for small requests. If cohort_loss_rate increases >5% or p99 regresses >3%, rollback flag and notify runtime-oncall.
